identity.captured_title: You are the Deep Research source-base reviewer for NebulaMind's galaxy-evolution wiki rebuild. Queue item 14 of 20 Core review: Kewley, Lisa J.; Nicholls, David C.; & Sutherland, Ralph S. (2019), Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics, volume 57, pages 511-570, "Understanding Galaxy Evolution Through Emission Lines." Verified identity before submit: DOI 10.1146/annurev-astro-081817-051832; arXiv 1910.09730; ADS bibcode 2019ARA&A..57..511K. Mission Build an advisory-only, source-rich synthesis of what this review established, what remained debated, its quantitative diagnostic calibrations, and the primary literature most useful for NebulaMind's galaxy-evolution wiki. Cover UV, optical, and IR emission-line physics and diagnostics for excitation source, gas-phase metallicity/abundance, ionization parameter, ISM pressure, electron density, radiation hardness, star formation, AGN, shocks, diffuse ionized gas, abundance gradients, and redshift evolution. Safety and scope - Advisory/reference packet only. Do not edit a wiki, database, trust ledger, deployment, repository, or publication. - Treat the 2019 review as synthesis and as the source of clearly labeled new review calibrations, not as primary observational evidence. - Use only sources actually cited by or unmistakably part of this review's bibliography and published no later than 2019. - Exclude merely similar uncited papers, post-2019 results, browsing spillover, and unsupported prose. - Keep H II regions, integrated galaxies, resolved spaxels, narrow-line regions, shocks, and diffuse ionized gas distinct. - Distinguish direct-temperature, recombination-line, strong-line empirical, and photoionization-model abundance scales. - Carry atomic data, abundance pattern, dust/depletion, density, pressure, ionizing spectrum, geometry, optical depth, ionization parameter definition, and model grid with quantitative claims. - Do not mix diagnostic calibrations across their stated metallicity, redshift, density, ionization, excitation-source, or wavelength regimes. - Do not interpret BPT/UV/IR classification boundaries as pure causal labels when mixing, aperture, shocks, DIG, and composite excitation are possible. - Treat metallicity offsets between calibrations as scale differences unless a conversion is explicitly validated. - Keep local empirical sequences separate from high-redshift abundance and ionization conditions. Required atomic output 1. Review identity and scope map. 2. At least 12 established findings, each with stable ID REV14-E##, epistemic type, bounded statement, regime/boundary conditions, confidence, and source keys. 3. At least 8 open debates/tensions, each with ID REV14-D##, competing positions, why unresolved, and source keys. 4. At least 8 key measurements/model calibrations, each with ID REV14-N##, exact equation/line-ratio definition/value, units, ionization zone and regime, sample/model, uncertainty/status, and source keys. Include where supported: electron-temperature ratios, density doublets, ionization-parameter diagnostics, common optical BPT boundaries, UV and IR diagnostic combinations, strong-line metallicity indices, pressure/density conversions, and DIG/mixture effects. 5. At least 6 "what remained unknown in 2019" items, ID REV14-U##, why they matter, and the decisive observation/model improvement needed. 6. Primary-citation harvest of 40-80 useful cited papers, separated into measurements, photoionization/shock simulations or model grids, analytic/atomic/calibration papers, and supporting reviews. For each provide key REV14-P###, exact authors/year/journal/title, DOI or none, arXiv or none, ADS bibcode, role, review locator, and a one-sentence scientific boundary. 7. DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED quarantine for candidates not proven to be in the source base or with uncertain DOI/arXiv/ADS identity. State UNCITED_NOT_USABLE and never cite them in claims. 8. Composite identity ledger for the review and every usable source. Flag duplicates, errata, conference-only context, diagnostic versions, atomic-data dependencies, calibration-scale conflicts, sample/aperture mismatches, and method-context-only sources. Quality bar - DOI, arXiv ID, and ADS bibcode must resolve to the same physical paper. - No inferred title/identifier hybrids; use exact identities. - Load-bearing measurements cite primary sources; the review may support synthesis or explicitly new 2019 review calibrations. - Every line ratio defines numerator/denominator and wavelength convention where ambiguity exists. - Every abundance claim specifies element and scale, normally 12+log(O/H), plus calibration family. - Every density/pressure claim specifies tracer/ionization zone and temperature assumptions. - Every model-derived claim states the relevant model family or grid boundary. - Supporting reviews do not count toward the primary-paper total. - Quarantined sources never appear in claim source lists. - Missing identifiers are "none," never guessed. Return one self-contained packet ending exactly with: REVIEW_BASE_14_DR_COMPLETE_REFERENCE_ONLY
